label: RML Lucknow ICU blood cultures (2022–23)
extraction_notes: Cureus 2024;16(3):e57356, RML Lucknow, ICU blood cultures, June 2022-June 2023, 669 samples, 213 (31.8%) growth. Susceptibility data is in bar-chart figures (Figure 1 gram-positive, Figure 2 gram-negative), NOT text tables; extracted the printed data-labels from the embedded chart images (rendered via pymupdf). Charts report %SUSCEPTIBLE (sensitivity), so from_R=false throughout. Enterococcus reported as 'Enterococcus species' (not split) -> mapped to canonical 'Enterococcus'; clindamycin bar for Enterococcus had no printed value so omitted. Acinetobacter reported as 'Acinetobacter species' -> mapped to 'Acinetobacter baumannii' (core organism). Resistance-mechanism context (Table 2/text): MRSA 77.6% of S. aureus (cefoxitin S=22.4 matches), methicillin-resistant CoNS 66%; overall MBL producers 64.3% of gram-negatives (Acinetobacter 71%, K. pneumoniae 65.9%, P. aeruginosa 68.4%, E. coli 60%); ESBL 19.6% overall (K. pneumoniae 26.8%). VITEK 2 / CLSI M100 2022. Testing was for cefoxitin, erythromycin, clindamycin, tetracycline, ciprofloxacin, chloramphenicol, vancomycin, linezolid, gentamicin, teicoplanin, ampicillin-sulbactam, ceftazidime, imipenem, piperacillin-tazobactam, amikacin.
missing_important: CoNS (Coagulase-negative Staphylococci), n=46 — the single most common isolate in the study — has a full antibiogram in Figure 1 (cefoxitin 34, erythromycin 15.2, clindamycin 28.3, tetracycline 65.2, ciprofloxacin 17.4, chloramphenicol 65.2, vancomycin 100, linezolid 100, gentamicin 55, teicoplanin 71.3) but is entirely omitted from the extraction.

label: Govt Doon Dehradun CSOM ear discharge (2022–24)

drugs.note: reported in Discussion text (57.8%, 26 isolates), not in Table 2

extraction_notes: Cureus 2024 (16(9):e69525), Sammal et al., Govt Doon Medical College, Dehradun; CSOM middle-ear pus, VITEK-2 / CLSI. Susceptibility tables read from PDF text (Tables 2-4, pages 5-6). Source prints Sensitive/Intermediate/Resistant as counts and %; I extracted %Sensitive only (I% NOT added). Total 129 culture-positive isolates. Only P. aeruginosa (Table 2) and S. aureus (Table 3) had full antibiograms; MRSA had a separate table (Table 4) but maps to the same canonical S. aureus so is listed in unmapped rather than merged. MRSA context: 18 MRSA + 23 S. aureus isolates => MRSA ~43.9% of all S. aureus (13.1% of 137 total cases / of 129 positives). AST denominators vary slightly by drug (e.g. piptazo n=38, ceftazidime n=45, imipenem n=44) but % taken exactly as printed. Amikacin for P. aeruginosa (57.8%) is from Discussion narrative, not Table 2.

label: SGRD Amritsar Klebsiella VAP (2018 & 2022)
extraction_notes: Source: Sharma et al., Cureus 2023;15(3):e36317, SGRD Amritsar, North India. Only K. pneumoniae studied (82 ETA isolates from mechanically ventilated ICU/VAP patients: 40 in Jan-Jun 2018, 42 in Jan-Jun 2022). Data taken from Table 2 (page 3), 'Antibiotic sensitivity pattern in 2018 and 2022', which reports n(%) SENSITIVE — these are %S values, extracted directly (from_R=false throughout). Returned as two organism entries (one per year). Column values verified as susceptibility (not resistance): confirmed against page 4 narrative (e.g. colistin sensitivity 92%->28%, meropenem 15%->2.5%, minocycline 67%->100%). Notable: colistin decline is the study's headline finding; XDR rose 62.5%->71% (from Table 3, page 4). Non-canonical drug tokens used: cefoperazonesulbactam (Cfs, printed abbrev; a combination not in the canonical cefoperazone entry), nalidixicacid. Minocycline 2018 count printed oddly as '26.8 (67%)'; used the 67%. TMP-SMX 2022 printed only as 50% with no isolate count. Ampicillin noted 100% resistant (0% S) both periods in narrative but NOT a row in Table 2, so omitted to avoid fabricating a table cell. No ESBL%/MRSA% figures reported; MDR/XDR classification counts are in Table 3 but not per-drug susceptibilities.

label: Hayes Prayagraj uropathogens (2018–19)

drugs.note: study reports 'Proteus sp.', species not specified

extraction_notes: Source: Bhargava et al., Front. Microbiol. 2022;13:965053 (Hayes Memorial Mission Hospital, Prayagraj UP). Data from Table 4 (page 6), text-extracted (machine-readable PDF, not scanned). Table 4 reports % susceptible (confirmed by Results text, e.g. 'amikacin was effective against 77.0% of E. coli'; 'imipenem outperformed meropenem by inhibiting 57.4% E. coli'). All values entered as printed %S; no %R conversion needed (from_R=false throughout). NT = not tested (cell omitted). Specimen = clean-catch midstream urine; study period Nov 2018–Dec 2019; 96.0% of isolates MDR. ESBL context: 40.4% of E. coli were ESBL producers; none of K. pneumoniae were ESBL. n per organism from Table 4 column headers. Proteus sp. mapped to Proteus mirabilis (species not specified in study — note added). Enterococcus not split to species → 'Enterococcus'. 'H-gentamycin' (high-concentration gentamicin, Enterococcus 66.7%) recorded as separate token h-gentamicin. Non-canonical drugs kept with lowercase tokens: novobiocin. S. epidermidis (n=8) reported but not in canonical organism list — see unmapped. No A. baumannii in study.
verify_issues: Organism naming over-specification: the extraction labels the second organism 'Proteus mirabilis', but Table 4 and the text report only 'Proteus sp.' (species not identified). All 14 susceptibility values map correctly to the Proteus column; only the top-level name is over-specified. The extraction includes a note acknowledging this, but the displayed name 'Proteus mirabilis' is not supported by the source and could mislead clinically.

No %R->%S conversion issues found: Table 4 prints susceptibility (%S) directly (confirmed by narrative on p5, e.g. vancomycin 100% S. aureus, nitrofurantoin 94.4% Enterococcus, chloramphenicol 83.3/75.0/87.5). All from_R:false flags are correct.

S. aureus clindamycin s:55.0 is ambiguous in the source (only two values, 55.0% and 62.5%, appear in the clindamycin row across the three gram-positive columns). Accepted as correct because clindamycin is clinically tested against staphylococci (not enterococci, which are intrinsically resistant), making S. aureus 55.0% / S. epidermidis 62.5% the consistent reading; the extraction correctly omits clindamycin for Enterococcus.
missing_important: Staphylococcus epidermidis (n=8) is a full organism column in Table 4 but is entirely omitted from the extraction. Its cells: Nitrofurantoin 100.0, Penicillin 12.5, Cefoxitin 25.0, Norfloxacin 37.5, Ciprofloxacin 37.5, Clindamycin 62.5, Erythromycin 25.0, Netilmicin 75.0, Novobiocin 87.5, Doxycycline 50.0, Vancomycin 100.0, Chloramphenicol 87.5 (all %S). May be an intentional exclusion given small n, but noting the omission.

label: JPNATC AIIMS Delhi Acinetobacter (2012–16)
extraction_notes: Source: Kumari et al., J Lab Physicians 2019;11:34-8, JPNATC AIIMS Delhi, 5-year surveillance 2012-2016. Table 1 (page 3) is the pooled antibiogram for Acinetobacter spp. (98.5% A. baumannii, 1.4% A. lwoffii, 0.1% A. hemolyticus) — mapped whole table to Acinetobacter baumannii per the dominant species. Table prints yearly R counts(%), plus 'Total resistance (%)' and 'Total sensitive (%)' pooled columns. I used the printed 'Total sensitive (%)' column directly as s (from_R=false). Colistin is not in Table 1; text states only 68 (1.8%) of 3744 isolates were colistin resistant by VITEK 2, so s=98.2 (from_R=true) — authors note these could not be retested by microbroth dilution. n=3744 total Acinetobacter isolates (28.9% of 16,210). Tigecycline was N/A in 2012 (pooled S from 2013-2016). Note: absolute counts in Table 1 sum to ~4680 (exceed 3744 isolates) — likely a per-isolate-test tally inconsistency in the source; percentages are internally consistent and were used. Drugs NOT tested (per authors): ampicillin/sulbactam, minocycline, cefoperazone/sulbactam.

label: MG Jaipur bloodstream infections (2022–23)
extraction_notes: Text-extracted (pypdf) from JLP 2024;16(4):501-506, Purohit et al, MGMC&H Jaipur BSI study. Values are % SUSCEPTIBLE — both tables headed "Antimicrobial susceptibility pattern ... (%)", confirmed by narrative (VAN/LZ/DAP 100% in S. aureus; oxacillin 43.5%S ≈ 100−56.5% MRSA). No %R conversion needed (from_R false everywhere). Table 1 = Gram-positive (cols P OX GEN HLG CIP LE TE COT E CD VAN TEI LZ DAP); Table 2 = Gram-negative (cols CAZ CPM ATR MRP IPM P/T CFS GEN AK CIP LE MIN CL(I) COT CXM CTR ETP AMC). Cells marked NT (not tested) or IR (intrinsically resistant) were omitted, not recorded as 0. Colistin column header explicitly notes (I)=intermediate but value 100 recorded as printed; colistin 100%S across all GNB matches scope hint. Klebsiella spp. mapped to K. pneumoniae (text: K. pneumoniae predominant), Acinetobacter spp.→A. baumannii, Pseudomonas spp.→P. aeruginosa (table labels were 'spp.'). Enterococcus reported combined in table (n=125) though text notes E. faecium 85%/E. faecalis 12.8% — used canonical 'Enterococcus'. CRE 50.2% (269/536), MRSA 56.5% (26/46), VRE 7.2% (9/125) per abstract/results. Non-canonical drug tokens used: penicillin, oxacillin, hlgentamicin (high-level gentamicin), cefoperazonesulbactam (cefoperazone-sulbactam, distinct from cefoperazone).
missing_important: Klebsiella/E.coli/Acinetobacter/Pseudomonas each have several NT (not tested) or IR (intrinsically resistant) cells in Table 2 that were correctly omitted (e.g., Klebsiella CAZ=NT, LE=NT, MIN=NT; Acinetobacter CXM/CTR/ETP/AMC=IR; Pseudomonas GEN/AK=NT, COT=IR) — no action needed, noting for completeness
S. aureus HLG=NT and Enterococcus OX=NT/GEN=IR/COT=IR/CD=IR in Table 1 correctly omitted

label: AIIMS Delhi medicine wards & ICU (2017–19)
extraction_notes: Source: Vaithiyam et al., J Lab Physicians 2020;12(3):196-202, AIIMS New Delhi medicine wards & ICU. Text extracted via pypdf (no page-image OCR needed; born-digital PDF). Data taken from Table 4 (Gram-negative) and Table 5 (Gram-positive), both explicitly headed 'Antimicrobial RESISTANCE patterns (%)'. ALL values are %R and were converted to %S = 100 - R (from_R:true on every cell). Confirmation that columns are resistance: colistin = 0 for all GNB, matching narrative 'colistin (no resistance)', and A. baumannii shows ~99-100 for cipro/cefotaxime/ceftazidime consistent with the reported 89% P-XDR. NOTE: the page-4 narrative loosely quotes the resistance numbers ('susceptibility to ... cefoperazone/sulbactam (34.7%)' and 'imipenem (43%)') while actually citing the %R table values — the tables are the authoritative resistance figures used here. n per organism from Table 2 (A.baumannii 92, K.pneumoniae 86, E.coli 75, P.aeruginosa 22, E.faecium 15, S.aureus 10; note isolate counts differ slightly from Table 4/5 denominators as tables include NT cells). Cef-Sul = cefoperazone/sulbactam (non-canonical; token cefoperazonesulbactam). 'Peni'=penicillin (token penicillin). NT (not tested) cells omitted: P.aeruginosa amoxiclav; E.faecium amoxiclav & amikacin; S.aureus tetracycline; Salmonella most drugs. MRSA context: methicillin resistance in 70% of S. aureus (7/10). ESBL% not reported. Overall ~90% of isolates drug-resistant, 61% P-XDR (Table 2 totals). Study year not printed in extracted text (filename indicates 2017-19); year left null to avoid fabrication. E. faecalis (n=2) and Salmonella spp. lacked mappable/prioritized drug rows — see unmapped.

label: SRM Chennai carbapenem resistance (2022–24)
extraction_notes: Text-readable PDF (Frontiers in Medicine 2025, DOI 10.3389/fmed.2025.1571231), SRM Chennai, Jul 2022-Jul 2024, 8,359 non-duplicate GNB; 24% (2,007) carbapenem-resistant. CRITICAL CAVEAT: All susceptibility values extracted apply ONLY to the carbapenem-resistant (CRO) subset, NOT to all clinical isolates — section 3.6 and Figure 5 explicitly report 'resistance patterns of CROs to various antibacterial agents.' So these %S are far lower than a general antibiogram; the n values used (E.coli 433, K.pneumoniae 733, P.aeruginosa 290, A.baumannii 388) are the carbapenem-resistant isolate counts. Source reports %RESISTANT throughout; I converted every cell to %S = 100 - R (from_R:true). Values taken from narrative text on page 5 (section 3.6); Figure 5 is a heat map image (not machine-readable) and Supplementary Table 2 is not in this PDF, so only the explicitly-printed numeric %R values were extracted. E.coli: CAZ 100%R, TZP 100%R, CIP 98.3%R, FEP 98.3%R, colistin 6.77%R, gentamicin 49.15%R. K.pneumoniae: CAZ 96%R, CIP 94.4%R, FEP 95.2%R, LEV 92.9%R. P.aeruginosa: CIP 94%R, TZP 88%R. A.baumannii: CAZ 96.2%R, TZP 96.2%R, CIP 94.9%R, colistin 7.5%R. Citrobacter and Proteus were described only qualitatively ('moderate'/'notable' resistance) with no numbers, so omitted. Carbapenem (IPM/MEM) susceptibility of the subset is 0% by definition (all resistant) and not extracted as antibiogram cells. Carbapenem-resistance prevalence by organism (from Results/Fig1): A.baumannii 48% (388/808), K.pneumoniae 38.6% (733/1897), P.aeruginosa 24.18% (290/1199), Proteus 24.1% (126/522), E.coli 12.1% (433/3577), Citrobacter 10.39% (37/356). AST by VITEK 2. No MRSA/ESBL data (GNB-only study).

extraction_notes:
Source: Neelambike Sumana et al., Front. Microbiol. 2025 (JSS Medical College, Mysuru, Karnataka; 1800-bed tertiary care hospital). Retrospective, VITEK-2, CLSI. Scope: K. pneumoniae from URINE only (920 isolates over 2014-2023). This is the ONLY organism with AST data; other uropathogens (E. coli n=9211, Enterococci, P. aeruginosa n=1108, A. baumannii n=192, S. aureus n=161, Proteus) are named with isolate counts only, NO susceptibility data given, so they are not extracted.

CRITICAL DATA-INTEGRITY ISSUE: In Tables 3 and 4 the S and R column headers are SWAPPED/mislabeled. The column labeled 'S' actually holds %RESISTANT. Verified against the paper's own narrative (pp.3,8) and CRKP counts, e.g. table 'S' for carbapenems 2023 = 38.55% while narrative explicitly states carbapenem RESISTANCE 2023 = 38.55% (32/83); same swap confirmed for every drug/year checked (fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, amoxiclav, piptazo, all cephalosporins, cotrimoxazole). Therefore true %susceptible = the table's 'R' column = 100 - narrative resistance. All s-values here are DERIVED from the reliable narrative resistance figures (from_R=true).

Data is reported PER YEAR (2014-2023), no per-drug pooled decade figure is printed. I extracted the most recent full year, 2023 (n=83), as the current antibiogram snapshot. If earlier years are needed the resistance values are (converting to S=100-R): e.g. 2014 (n=27) carbapenem R 3.70% (S 96.30%), ceftriaxone R 7.41% (S 92.59%), rising steeply over the decade. Decade-pooled carbapenem resistance = 41.84% (385/920 CRKP), matching the scope hint; carbapenem resistance peaked 66.13% in 2021 then fell to 38.55% by 2023.

Carbapenems reported as a single class (footnote: ertapenem+imipenem+meropenem) — I duplicated the 61.45% across all three keys with a note that it is not species/agent-specific. 'Fluroquinolones' footnoted as ciprofloxacin. 'Aminoglycosides' is a class with no specific agent named (mapped to generic 'aminoglycosides' token). Cefoperazone/sulbactam and cefuroxime-axetil use descriptive tokens as they are not exact canonical keys.

extraction_notes: Source: Muthusamy R, Mahesh S, Travasso C. 'Antibiotic Profiling of E. coli Borne UTI Infection in Tertiary Healthcare Settings.' Cureus 16(3):e56632, 2024 (Saveetha Medical College, Chennai). Text extracted with PyMuPDF (6 pages, digital text, fully readable). Study: 80 urine samples from female patients (35-50 yr), 44 UTI-positive, 18 E. coli-positive. ONLY quantitative AST is Table 1 (page 3): zone-of-inhibition in mm for FOUR individual E. coli strains (1B2602, 1B2453, 1B2695, 1R578) with legend '* Sensitive, -- Resistant' (bare numbers without asterisk are ambiguous/not flagged sensitive). This is NOT a percentage-susceptible antibiogram: no %S or %R is printed for any drug across the 18 isolates, and per-drug denominators are only 1-4 strains with inconsistent/partial testing. I therefore did NOT compute or emit any numeric s values (would require fabricating a population statistic from n<=4). All s set null; q captures the printed per-strain qualitative verdict where clear. Methods section names only nitrofurantoin/cephalosporin/cephalexin discs (contradicting the wider drug list in Table 1) and states high resistance to these three, but gives no numeric value. Study is low quality and internally inconsistent (includes gram-positive-only drugs like vancomycin/linezolid/erythromycin/penicillin against E. coli). No MRSA%/ESBL% quantitative data; abstract mentions 'ESBL EA' strain identifiers and text quotes '91% multidrug resistance' but that figure is cited from another region (China), not this cohort. Reporting classified 'mixed' (per-strain qualitative S/R via disc zones). reads_ok=true.
missing_important: Cefdinir (CD): present in Table 1 (1B2602=24* sensitive, 1B2453=16 no*, 1B2695/1R578 not tested) but omitted from extraction; per-strain only, no population %S — omission is defensible.
Linezolid (LZ), Erythromycin (E), Penicillin (P), Vancomycin (VA): Gram-positive-oriented discs present in Table 1 but not relevant to E. coli reporting; correctly omitted.

label: Andhra MC Vizag UTI GNB (2022–23)
extraction_notes: PDF read successfully via PyMuPDF (3 pages, text-based, not scanned). The Read tool failed (poppler not installed) but text extraction worked. This paper (Pydi et al., Andhra Medical College, Visakhapatnam; Int J Curr Pharm Res 2024) does NOT contain any numeric antibiogram table. Table 1 gives isolate counts/percentages (n=858 total: 839 GNB + 19 GPC); Table 2 is a comparative isolate-frequency table vs other studies; Fig. 1 gives MDR isolate counts per organism. NO per-organism per-antibiotic %S or %R values are printed anywhere, so every organism has an empty drugs array (counts recorded as metadata only). The only susceptibility info is QUALITATIVE and applies to the pooled MDR-GNB subset (177/839 = 20.62% MDR), NOT to individual organisms: MDR GNB were resistant to cephalosporins (ceftazidime, cefixime, ceftriaxone, ceftazidime+clavulanic acid), carbapenems (imipenem, meropenem), and quinolones (ciprofloxacin, norfloxacin, nalidixic acid, ofloxacin, levofloxacin), and 'most were sensitive to fosfomycin and nitrofurantoin.' These are group-level words without numbers and not mappable to a single canonical organism, so they were deliberately NOT recorded as drug cells to avoid attributing pooled-MDR resistance to specific organisms. MDR breakdown (Fig.1, of 177): E. coli 97 (54.8%), Klebsiella 54 (30.5%), Acinetobacter 13 (7.3%), Pseudomonas 7 (4%), Proteus 5 (2.8%), Citrobacter 1 (0.56%). Klebsiella/Acinetobacter/Pseudomonas/Proteus/Citrobacter were reported at genus level ('spp'); mapped to canonical binomials as closest matches. CLSI 2022 breakpoints, Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion.
verify_issues: The source paper contains NO per-organism per-drug antibiotic susceptibility table (no %S or %R values). It only reports isolate counts (Table 1), an MDR breakdown (Fig. 1), and a comparative isolate-frequency table (Table 2). Susceptibility is described only qualitatively in prose. The extraction's empty drugs[] arrays correctly reflect this — no susceptibility cells were fabricated.

Organism counts all match Table 1 exactly: E. coli 435, Klebsiella 232, Acinetobacter 105, Pseudomonas 55, Proteus 10, Citrobacter 2, Staph aureus 17, Enterococcus 2. Specimen (urine) and study period (Aug 2022 - Jan 2023) also correct.

Naming over-specification (not in source, an unsupported inference): source lists genus/'spp' level only. Extraction names 'Klebsiella pneumoniae' (source: 'Klebsiella spp'), 'Acinetobacter baumannii' (source: 'Acinetobacter spp'), 'Pseudomonas aeruginosa' (source: 'Pseudomonas spp'), 'Proteus mirabilis' (source: 'Proteus spp'). No susceptibility data hangs off these names, so no clinical impact, but the species assignments are not supported by the paper.

extraction_notes: Padmaja et al., Bioinformation 21(6):1475-1480 (2025), KIMS Amalapuram ICU (MICU/SICU/CCIU), Jun 2023-Jul 2024. Text-extractable PDF (PyMuPDF), 6 pages. Source reports susceptibility ONLY as qualitative bands: highly sensitive >=80%, moderately sensitive 60-80%, poorly sensitive <60% (Table 3, page 4). No S/I/R counts, no exact per-drug percentages EXCEPT Tobramycin vs Acinetobacter = 96% (only exact figure printed). For 60-80% bands I stored midpoint s=70 with approx:true; for <60% bands I left s=null and used qualitative q (no lower bound given, so a number would be a guess); for the single 'carbapenems strong 80%' Pseudomonas statement I stored s=80 approx. 'Carbapenems' is a class - only meropenem was tested (methods: 'Meropenem and minocycline used as reserved drugs'), so mapped to meropenem with note. 'Cephalosporins (1st-3rd gen)' is a class - recorded as ceftazidime + ceftriaxone (the named first-line cephalosporins) with note. Cefoperazone-sulbactam and ceftazidime-avibactam kept as printed combo tokens (not plain cefoperazone/ceftazidime). n values are Table-2 TOTAL ICU isolate counts per genus (E.coli 244, Klebsiella 277, Pseudomonas 148, Acinetobacter 93, Proteus 13); Table 3's susceptibility is titled 'urinary isolates' but gives no urine-specific n, so specimen noted as urine/ICU with this caveat. Klebsiella genus mapped to K. pneumoniae; Acinetobacter to A. baumannii; Pseudomonas to P. aeruginosa; Proteus to P. mirabilis (species not explicitly stated by paper). INTERNAL CONTRADICTIONS in source: (1) nitrofurantoin for Klebsiella listed 'effective' in Table 3/discussion but 'low sensitivity' in page-3 narrative - I followed Table 3; (2) nitrofurantoin/norfloxacin for Pseudomonas & Acinetobacter listed as 'effective urinary drug' in Table 3 and page-4 text, but page-3 text says 'inadequate sensitivity' - given clinical implausibility (nitrofurantoin has no Pseudomonas/Acinetobacter activity) and the conflict, I OMITTED these two agents for Pseudomonas and Acinetobacter rather than record a likely-erroneous value; recorded them for Proteus only as ineffective (<60%). Enterobacter (n=15, 0% resistant) and single Stenotrophomonas/Burkholderia isolates had no per-drug AST reported, so omitted. Table 2 also gives MDR/XDR/PDR resistance-category counts (not drug-specific susceptibilities) - not extracted as drug cells.
verify_issues: This is a banded/qualitative antibiogram, not numeric. Table 3 gives ranges (>=80% highly, 60-80% moderately, <60% poorly). The extraction represents the 60-80% band as s=70 (midpoint) and flags approx=true; the 80% cell (Pseudomonas carbapenems) as s=80; and <60% cells as s=null. This is a defensible modeling choice but no exact percentages exist in the source except Tobramycin/Acinetobacter (96%).

SOURCE INTERNAL CONFLICT (E. coli, cefoperazone-sulbactam): Table 3 lists cefoperazone-sulbactam under E. coli's <60% (poorly sensitive) column, but the page-3 narrative states 'cefoperazone-sulbactam, other reserved agents such as carbapenems and minocycline exhibited moderate sensitivity (60-80%)' for E. coli. The extraction followed Table 3 (s=null, <60%), which is the correct primary tabular source, but the contradiction should be noted.

SOURCE INTERNAL CONFLICT (Klebsiella, nitrofurantoin): Table 3 lists Nitrofurantoin as the effective urinary drug for Klebsiella, but page-3 narrative says 'nitrofurantoin showed low sensitivity.' Extraction followed Table 3 (effective) and explicitly documents the conflict. Acceptable.

SOURCE INTERNAL CONFLICT (Pseudomonas & Acinetobacter urinary agents): Table 3 lists Nitrofurantoin+Norfloxacin as effective urinary drugs for both Pseudomonas and Acinetobacter, and page-4 narrative agrees ('effective against Pseudomonas and Acinetobacter'), yet page-3 narrative says these agents 'showed inadequate sensitivity'/'demonstrated limited efficacy' for these organisms. Extraction omitted nitrofurantoin/norfloxacin from Pseudomonas and Acinetobacter entirely (see missing_important). No value error, but an inconsistency versus how E. coli/Klebsiella nitrofurantoin was handled.

MINOR over-specification: the paper names organisms only at genus level for the ICU cohort (Klebsiella, Pseudomonas, Acinetobacter, Proteus). The extraction assigns species (K. pneumoniae, P. aeruginosa, A. baumannii, P. mirabilis). These are reasonable inferences (species named elsewhere in discussion) but are not stated for the antibiogram itself. No susceptibility impact.

All n values, band assignments, and drug mappings verified correct against Table 2 and Table 3. Meropenem <60% for Acinetobacter (explicit in Table 3 poorly-sensitive column), Tobramycin 96% for Acinetobacter, and Pseudomonas carbapenems 80% are all accurately captured. No hallucinated cells and no %R<->%S direction errors.
missing_important: Pseudomonas: Table 3 lists Nitrofurantoin and Norfloxacin as effective urinary drugs (extraction omitted both). Note conflicting page-3 narrative.
Acinetobacter: Table 3 lists Nitrofurantoin and Norfloxacin as effective urinary drugs (extraction omitted both). Note conflicting page-3 narrative.

extraction_notes: Source: TARS-Net Telangana State AMR Surveillance Annual Report 2024 (nodal centre Osmania Medical College), 13 sentinel sites, 10 districts, 16,274 isolates (15,674 unique-patient after dedup), Jan 1–Dec 31 2024. Tables report %RESISTANT (%R) per specimen column; ALL s-values here were converted s=100−R (from_R:true). Guidelines: CLSI. Specimen scope for each organism entry is the table's per-specimen N (BLOOD or URINE). I extracted blood (sterile-site benchmark) for all six core organisms, plus urine for E. coli, Klebsiella and Enterococcus (UTI-relevant). Tables 6–11 = S.aureus/Enterococcus/E.coli/Klebsiella/Pseudomonas/Acinetobacter. Report labels genus-level "Klebsiella species", "Pseudomonas species", "Acinetobacter species", "Enterococcus species" (species not split) — mapped to K. pneumoniae / P. aeruginosa / A. baumannii as the dominant species and to generic "Enterococcus". MRSA context: cefoxitin %R (methicillin surrogate) = 53% in blood, 43% in pus, 100% in OSBF(n=4) for S. aureus; so MRSA ~53% among blood isolates. VRE: Enterococcus vancomycin %R = 3% blood, 0.26% urine, 2% pus. Linezolid 0%R across all specimens for both S.aureus and Enterococcus. Colistin 0%R (100%S) for all gram-negatives across all specimens. DATA-QUALITY CAVEAT (safety-critical): E. coli URINE column (Table 8, N=4775) is internally inconsistent — urine shows HIGHER resistance than blood for carbapenems/aminoglycosides/nitrofurantoin (imipenem 64%R urine vs 7% blood; meropenem 35 vs 11; amikacin 88 vs 21; gentamicin 89 vs 26; nitrofurantoin 81; piptazo 74 vs 31), which is biologically implausible and opposite the normal pattern (and opposite Klebsiella's own table where urine<blood). These urine E.coli cells are flagged with note fields and are very likely source data-entry/column errors; treat with caution or exclude downstream. Cefotaxime for E.coli urine (35%R) is lower than blood (85%R) — also inverted. Klebsiella and Enterococcus urine columns look plausible (urine<blood). n reported per drug ("Number Tested") varies within each specimen; organism n set to the specimen header N. Also available but not extracted here: pus aspirate and OSBF columns for every organism (present in tables), and location-type (IN/OUT/ICU) resistance breakdowns in Figures 5–10.

extraction_notes: Source: Panigrahi et al., Cureus 2025;17(10):e94006 (KIMS Bhubaneswar). PDF read via PyMuPDF text extraction (pdftoppm/pdftotext unavailable). Data taken from Table 2 (page 10), which prints Sensitive/Intermediate/Resistant counts and percentages for each of 13 drugs across the whole study population and 4 subgroups (ICU, non-ICU, CAI, HAI). I extracted the overall Total (n=7,942) Sensitive % values as printed (%S only; Intermediate not added). Values match the abstract/text (tigecycline 74.79%S, gentamicin 39.45%S, meropenem 34.34%S, piptazo 32.44%S). Note the scope hint 'cipro 78.4%R' corresponds to the Resistant column (6,227, 78.40%R); the reported %S for ciprofloxacin is 19.08% (I:2.50%), so no %R conversion was needed as %S is printed directly. CPS = cefoperazone-sulbactam mapped to non-canonical token 'cefoperazonesulbactam' (distinct from plain cefoperazone). Only organism studied is K. pneumoniae; other Klebsiella species excluded by authors. Subgroup rows (ICU/non-ICU/CAI/HAI) also available in Table 2 but only the overall pooled figures extracted here. VITEK 2, CLSI 2022 breakpoints.

label: KIMS Bhubaneswar sterile body fluids (2021–22)

drugs.note: Derived from MRSA prevalence 48.9% (methicillin resistance); s=100-48.9

extraction_notes: Source: Poddar et al., Cureus 18(3):e104772 (2026), KIMS Bhubaneswar, Odisha; retrospective sterile-body-fluid antibiogram, Jan 2021-Dec 2022. 2307 samples, 291 isolates (12.6% positive); GPC 54%, S. aureus most common (92/291), MRSA 48.9%; K. pneumoniae top GNB (40), E. coli (27), Acinetobacter (24), Pseudomonas (19). All susceptibility data are presented ONLY as unlabeled bar charts (Fig 1 = Gram-positive: S. aureus, CONS, Enterococcus; Fig 2 = Gram-negative: K. pneumoniae, E. coli, Pseudomonas spp., Acinetobacter spp.) plus narrative sentences. There are NO numeric susceptibility tables. Method: rendered figure pages with PyMuPDF at 6x, calibrated the y-axis from detected tick-label centers (Fig 2: 0%=y1383, 100%=y368; Fig 1 baseline y1504), then extracted each bar's top and mid-bar color programmatically. Color->drug map validated by matching extracted values to the paper's own text (Acinetobacter imipenem 41.9 vs 'imipenem 41%', gentamicin 41.5 vs 'aminoglycosides 41%', cotrimoxazole 36.8 vs '37.5%', ciprofloxacin 36.8 vs '38%'; E. coli ciprofloxacin 10.8 vs 'ciprofloxacin resistance high 90%'; Pseudomonas ceftazidime 20.9 vs '21%', ciprofloxacin 9.9 vs '10-11%'). Values are % SUSCEPTIBLE. GNB values all flagged approx (read from bar chart, ~1-2% precision). Gram-positive: the tigecycline/linezolid/daptomycin/vancomycin/teicoplanin/high-level-gentamicin figures are stated verbatim in the text (not approx); the lower bars (penicillin, gentamicin, clindamycin, ciprofloxacin, erythromycin, cotrimoxazole) are read off the chart (approx). Text attributes the high staph values to 'Staphylococcus spp.' but the chart plots S. aureus as a distinct group separate from CONS and the numbers match the S. aureus bars, so mapped to S. aureus. S. aureus oxacillin/cloxacillin s=51.1 derived from MRSA 48.9% (from_R). Pseudomonas spp. mapped to P. aeruginosa (discussion names P. aeruginosa in synovial fluid); Acinetobacter spp. mapped to A. baumannii (named in discussion/conclusion). Pseudomonas AMP/AMC/imipenem and Acinetobacter AMP/AMC/ceftriaxone bars were not detectable (intrinsic resistance / near-zero) and were omitted rather than guessed. Overall GNB MDR/XDR/PDR 21.6%/14.2%/3%. CONS (coagulase-negative staph, 43 isolates) not in canonical list - omitted. Streptococcus pneumoniae/spp., Enterobacter, Citrobacter etc. had no per-organism antibiogram reported.
verify_issues: Staph aureus text-derived cells (linezolid 95.65, dapto 95, TGC 92, VA/TEI 90.21): the paper states these for 'Staphylococcus spp.' collectively (Fig 1 has separate S. aureus and CoNS bar groups). Assigning them specifically to S. aureus is a reasonable but not certain mapping; the 95.65% 'highest' value could belong to either Staph group.

Pseudomonas amikacin s=20.9 is read as LOWER than meropenem/cefepime (25.9), but the text explicitly says Pseudomonas showed 'highest sensitivity to amikacin, followed by carbapenems' — i.e., amikacin should exceed the carbapenems. Bar-read ordering is inconsistent with the text; value is approximate so not force-corrected, but flag for review.

Klebsiella ampicillin s=41.9 (bar read) is clinically implausible since K. pneumoniae is intrinsically ampicillin-resistant (expected ~0%); cannot confirm from the rendered bar chart. Possible misread of the AMP bar.
Oxacillin s=51.1 is a valid 100-R conversion from MRSA 48.9% (45/92); direction correct.

All remaining Gram-negative per-drug numbers are pixel reads off Figure 2 bar chart and cannot be independently confirmed to the stated decimal precision; they are appropriately flagged approx and are broadly consistent with the text ranges (amikacin 41-63%, carbapenems 40-60%, E. coli cipro ~10%).
missing_important: Streptococcus spp. (n=3) 100% sensitive to benzylpenicillin, daptomycin, gentamicin, linezolid, vancomycin (stated in text) — omitted, though n is very small.
CONS (coagulase-negative staphylococci, n=43) has its own susceptibility bar group in Figure 1 and is omitted from the extraction.

extraction_notes: Das PP et al., J Pure Appl Microbiol 2023;17(3):1591-1604. Assam Medical College & Hospital, Dibrugarh (institution-wide, AMRSN/ICMR site). Study period Oct 2018-Mar 2021. Text-extracted with pymupdf (Read tool could not render PDF; poppler not installed). All susceptibility data reported as %RESISTANT (R%) in Table 2 (Gram-negatives) and Table 3 (Gram-positives); every cell converted to %S = 100 - R with from_R:true. Table 2 organisms labelled Klebsiella spp./Proteus spp./Enterobacter spp. mapped to K. pneumoniae/P. mirabilis/E. cloacae with per-cell notes (Klebsiella predominantly K. pneumoniae per abstract). Citrobacter kept as genus. n values taken from Table 2 headers (Acinetobacter n=687, Pseudomonas n=646); note text on p.9 gives slightly different NFGNB counts (A. baumannii n=550, P. aeruginosa n=590). Cefepime, Tobramycin (except Pseudomonas), Minocycline (except Acinetobacter) etc. were ND (not done) for several organisms and omitted. Colistin: MIC-tested on only 261 pooled GN isolates, all susceptible (not organism-specific, so not added per organism). S. aureus vancomycin s=100 added because text states VRSA not detected. MRSA 44.7% = cefoxitin resistance. VRE overall 1.2% (10/817) is pooled across Enterococcus species, so vancomycin not added per E. faecalis/E. faecium. Nitrofurantoin & Fosfomycin tested on urine isolates only (CLSI). HLG = high-level gentamicin 120 µg for Enterococci. Mupirocin and Penicillin used as non-canonical lowercase tokens. Overall carbapenem-R: Enterobacteriaceae 58.8%, NFGNB 56.0%.

label: IGGMC Nagpur full antibiogram (2024–25)
extraction_notes: Cureus 2026 (Mohod et al.), IGGMC Nagpur; study period May 2024–April 2025; 4603 culture-positive isolates. Tables 2-4 (pages 6-8) report % RESISTANT — all s values converted as s=100-R (from_R:true). IR=intrinsic resistance, NR=not recommended by CLSI, NT=not tested, MIC=only MIC recommended, U=tested only in urinary isolates — these cells omitted or marked. E. coli/K. pneumoniae from Table 2 (lactose-fermenting GNB); P. aeruginosa/Acinetobacter from Table 3 (non-lactose-fermenters) — 'Acinetobacter spp.' mapped to Acinetobacter baumannii per scope. S. aureus/Enterococcus faecalis/faecium from Table 4. Colistin 0%R = 100%S all GNB. MRSA = 48.72% (matches S. aureus cefoxitin 48%R → 52%S). VRE 0.77%. Salmonella Typhi (n=11) figures from narrative prose on page 7 (not tabulated): ampicillin 78%R, cefotaxime 49%R, azithromycin 64%R, levofloxacin 64%R, cotrimoxazole 46%R. Nitrofurantoin/Fosfomycin tested only in urinary isolates. penicillin and high-level-gentamicin (hlg) use non-list tokens.

drugs.note: OPD+Ward pooled; ICU too few to report
OPD+Ward pooled; ICU too few to report
OPD+Ward pooled; ICU too few to report

extraction_notes:
SOURCE FILE WAS TRUNCATED: the delivered PDF (9,318,016 bytes) is an incomplete download — no xref/trailer/catalog/page-tree and only the first ~106 content pages survived (physical pages up to ~p71). I recovered it by scanning surviving objects with PyMuPDF, pairing each text content stream with its adjacent /Font resource dict, appending a synthetic Catalog+Pages tree, and repairing with qpdf; the reconstructed doc extracts real text via the fonts' ToUnicode CMaps (not OCR). Chapters 3+ (Enterobacterales trend tables, R&D chapters) fall beyond the truncation point and could NOT be read.

VALUES ARE POOLED FROM COUNTS: All %S values were computed by summing the S/tested counts across the OPD+Ward+ICU columns of the Chapter-2 specimen-wise tables (Section B), so they are exact pooled percentages, not read-off %. Sources by organism: E. coli / K. pneumoniae / A. baumannii / Salmonella Typhi = BLOOD (Tables 2.7, 2.8, 2.9, 2.10); P. aeruginosa = URINE (Table 2.13, no blood table survived); S. aureus = PUS/EXUDATES (Table 2.17); E. faecalis / E. faecium = URINE (Tables 2.14, 2.15). Salmonella Typhi table had only OPD+Ward columns (n=1061). Denominators validate against Table 1.2 isolate counts (e.g. E. coli blood 3244, K. pneumoniae blood 2909, P. aeruginosa urine 1184, E. faecalis urine 1595, E. faecium urine 942 all match). For S. aureus daptomycin/tigecycline/teicoplanin, ICU had counts flagged '-' (too few) so those three are OPD+Ward-only pools; all other S. aureus drugs include ICU.

MRSA%: cefoxitin S=47.8% in pus implies MRSA ~52%. Executive-summary reported MRSA ~50% in ICU, ~35% in ward isolates; vancomycin/teicoplanin ~100% vs MRSA; linezolid resistance very rare. ESBL/carbapenemase context: NDM-1 predominant in E. coli (34% of isolates), then OXA-1 18%, OXA-48 14%, CTX-M-15 12%; in K. pneumoniae SHV 50%, CTX-M-15 34%, OXA-48 29%. A. baumannii carbapenem resistance 88.0% (2023), OXA-23-like ~95% of carbapenem resistance. Enterococci overall vancomycin resistance 17.5% (E. faecium 29.6% vs E. faecalis 5.8%) — consistent with my urine-pooled vancomycin S (E. faecalis 94.7%, E. faecium 73.0%).

CROSS-CHECK vs all-sample national headline figures in the Executive Summary (scope 'all samples except faeces & urine', which differ slightly from my specimen-specific blood pools): E. coli 2023 piptazo 42.4%, amikacin 68.2%, imipenem 62.7%, meropenem 66.0%; K. pneumoniae 2023 piptazo 26.5%, imipenem 35.6%, meropenem 37.6%, ciprofloxacin 17.1%. These all-sample values run a few points off my blood pools (expected, different specimen mix). NOTE: the summary's P. aeruginosa ciprofloxacin/levofloxacin resistance numbers were textually identical to its carbapenem numbers (likely a copy-paste error), so I did NOT use them; P. aeruginosa values here are the exact urine-table pools instead.
missing_important: Not an error, but note: the ICMR-AMRSN 2023 source (Tables 2.7-2.17) does NOT print a single pooled susceptibility %. Each organism/drug is split into three care-setting columns (OPD='CPD', Ward, ICU='ICD') as fractions e.g. '277 / 367 (75.5%)'. The extraction correctly computed the pooled overall %S = sum(numerators)/sum(denominators) across the three columns, and the n = sum of the three column denominators. This was verified to match for all 81 cells.

The source additionally reports per-setting values (OPD/Ward/ICU) that the extraction collapses into one number; if setting-specific antibiograms are ever needed (e.g. ICU-specific carbapenem %S, which is markedly lower), that granularity exists in the source but is intentionally not captured here.

extraction_notes: Source: Gautam et al, Indian J Med Res 2019;149:208-215 (ICMR multi-centric ESBL study, 4 tertiary centres: AIIMS Delhi, PGIMER Chandigarh, CMC Vellore, JIPMER Puducherry; Oct 2014-Mar 2016). Study covers ONLY E. coli (341 isolates) and K. pneumoniae (304 isolates) — no P. aeruginosa, A. baumannii, S. aureus, or Enterococcus. Method: Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion, CLSI. Table II reports % SUSCEPTIBLE by centre; Table III reports % RESISTANT (n/N) split by ESBL-producer vs non-ESBL. I derived OVERALL susceptibility by pooling Table III ESBL + non-ESBL resistant counts per drug (s = 100 - pooled %R, from_R:true for all pooled cells). Colistin values taken directly from the printed overall figures in the Results text (E. coli 99% = 271/274; K. pneumoniae 98% = 229/234), not from R. CAVEAT: Table III denominators (e.g. 167+202=369 for E. coli, 98+126=224 for K. pneumoniae) exceed stated collection totals of 341/304, likely reflecting drug-specific tested subsets/classification; per-drug pooled %R is nevertheless computed directly from printed n/N. Individual per-centre susceptibility values are available in Table II if centre-level breakdown is preferred. ESBL prevalence context: CDT detected ESBL in 33% E. coli (98/298) and 42% K. pneumoniae (102/245). CFS-SUL = cefoperazone-sulbactam combination (mapped to token cefoperazone-sulbactam, not the plain cefoperazone key). CFD = cefpodoxime (no canonical key; token cefpodoxime). Rounded to 1 decimal.
